svg.title: E04 / AURA VERTICAL engineering mission profile
svg.desc: E04, AURA VERTICAL. Original project: A Measurement of the Concentration of Greenhouse Gases as Altitude Increases. Session E: ASCEND. Scientific question: Does a calibrated vertical gas profile contain an altitude-dependent mole-fraction signal beyond pressure, humidity, response lag and flight-path variability? Testable hypothesis: Pressure compensation and lag correction will change apparent gradients from inexpensive sensors; remaining gradients may differ between boundary-layer air and the free troposphere.. svg.text: A Measurement of the Concentration of Greenhouse Gases as Altitude Increases
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Make the greenhouse-gas balloon concept a traceable atmospheric profile
study. Report dry-air mole fraction separately from number density and raw
sensor voltage. Combine pressure, water vapor, temperature and response-time
corrections so a trend with altitude has a physical meaning; compare with
NOAA profiles before interpreting local atmospheric transport.
Does a calibrated vertical gas profile contain an altitude-dependent
mole-fraction signal beyond pressure, humidity, response lag and flight-path
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT

inexpensive sensors; remaining gradients may differ between boundary-layer
Calibrate over the actual pressure/temperature envelope; nominal room
Infer gas identity only from a selective calibrated analyzer; broad gas
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
NOAA flights are comparison observations, not contemporaneous ground truth
for Arizona. Balloon horizontal drift and diurnal boundary-layer change
